title: Lee Collins's fingering and how Armstrong played when Miller arrived
summary: They discuss Lee Collins's unusual fingering and his attempts to play like Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I don't think about that boy, but I ain't got much of him, he used to do like this, you know. Who's that? Lee Collins. Lee Collins.
Oh yeah, the way he fingered. I couldn't see how he could do that boy. He would finger it funny, huh?
I can't finger it like that. I can't finger it like that. I can't finger it like that. I can't say it like that.
I just messed up. He figures back on the first joint away from the hands. Right back there. Right there.
And I want to see how he could do to save my life.
And he played that order, that style on that. When did he play that style?

Like that? Mm-hmm. Oh, well, that's how he first started out, you know. But he got kind of, you know, trying to do, just like I said, trying to do the Lewis stuff, but it was too much for him, you know.
Yeah. How did Lewis play in those times?
When I first came here, Lewis did some nice playing. He used to play the thing, yeah. When I first came here, this is what he tried to trick everybody on.
